findings.reason: the section rests a scope decision on a premise its own cited path refutes, so the worker will meet a resolved backend at queue time and cannot tell whether to share the fourth refusal; the author must state the real reason (the launching lane may differ from the queued lane after admission rerouting) or reconsider sharing it.
findings.text: §2 says that because "a queued request has no such backend until the picker routes it" the execution-fit refusal is not shared, but `queue_requests` (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:293`) *requires* a lane (`backend_name` or the config's `local_backend`/`default_backend`, raising `queueing a request names no backend to queue it for` when neither is set) and `resolve_role` (`reckon/crew/routing.py:200`) resolves that lane's effective backend settings, role overlay included, with no picker involved — which is exactly where `plan_dispatch` reads `backend.get("execution_capable")` (`reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:840`) before `assess_execution_fit` at `:837`, so the backend the refusal needs exists at queue time

response_events.note: §2 now shares all four refusals: execution fit is judged against the lane the request is queued for, resolved by resolve_role (routing.py near line 200), which is the lane the admit service launches it on; a case covers it.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every line anchor in the changed unit resolves at or beside the number given: `validate_node` at `reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:843`, the execution-fit refusal at `:869`, `_DELIVERABLE_ACTIONS` at `reckon/crew/node.py:79` (and it contains `run`), and `gate_population_patterns` at `reckon/crew/node.py:1099`.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — the changed §2 now carries one case and one negative control per shared refusal, and its fifth case uses a glob `gate_population_patterns` actually keeps (`_GATE_POPULATION_IS_A_SET` at `reckon/crew/node.py:1096` requires `[?*\[]`, so `tests/test_missing_*.py` reaches the check while a literal file name would not).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every gate log is placed under the run directory, which is durable, rather than a session scratchpad or a node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test path names the behaviour it measures, and no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag reaches a symbol, file name or comment in the unit.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §2 justifies leaving the execution-fit refusal at launch on a claim about the queue path that the queue path itself contradicts.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — the deliverable is one mechanism (share the three node-local refusals and call it from both paths); the explicit exclusion of the execution-fit refusal is a scope boundary on that mechanism, not a second deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `plan-section-depends-on` makes both file-sharing units declare their wait on s2 (`s3` and `s5` share `reckon/crew/dispatch.py` and `reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py`), s4 writes `reckon/_store.py` alone and is independent, and `plan-after` names the finished predecessor `a-dry-run-must-resolve-what-the-real-call-resolves`.
